title: Vortex topological charge: winding, fluxoid and magnetic flux
summary: Distinguish real-space winding from measured flux, retain screening and junction constraints, and compare quantization claims with the original experiments.

review.scope: Original Deaver and Doll scans, selected Abrikosov and final Bauer passages, the original Tsuei abstract, and independent winding/inductance examples.
limitations: Complete scientific acceptance and experimental raw-data audits remain open.
The full Byers–Yang proof, 1994 tricrystal analysis and Bardeen–Stephen derivation have not been reviewed.
The single-junction and lumped-ring examples do not reproduce a multijunction experiment or all fractional-vortex manifolds.
The final Bauer passages were compared selectively with the author version; a complete version comparison remains open.

references.title: Nobel Lecture: Type-II superconductors and the vortex lattice

verification.note: Selected pages 976–977 were reread: phase zeros and winding, gauge-invariant gradient, flux per unit cell, average induction and isotropic versus crystal-dependent lattice geometry. This is the original author’s later lecture, not a full independent microscopic derivation.

references.title: Experimental Evidence for Quantized Flux in Superconducting Cylinders

verification.note: Published 15 July 1961. Original pages 43–46 and Figures 1–2 were visually read: tin cylinders, calibration, first-step uncertainty of about 20 percent, extra geometry uncertainty if the copper correction fails, and finite response time. No raw-data reanalysis was performed.

references.title: Experimental Proof of Magnetic Flux Quantization in a Superconducting Ring

verification.note: Published 15 July 1961. Original pages 51–52 were visually read. This report compares an observed step interval near 0.2 Oe with a predicted 0.5 Oe using hc/e and calls the discrepancy unexplained. Do not replace that original quantitative statement with a later historical summary.

references.title: Theoretical Considerations Concerning Quantized Magnetic Flux in Superconducting Cylinders

verification.note: Published 15 July 1961. The opening on page 46 was visually read in the preceding experimental-paper scan. The remaining proof was not retrieved. The Wiki London and ring equations are explicitly derived under their own assumptions, not attributed to a completed review of this paper.

references.title: On the Magnetic Properties of Superconductors of the Second Group

verification.note: Selected pages 1177 and 1180 were read as extracted text. The early triangular-lattice estimate differs from the later author lecture; the original scan is not treated as proof of the modern minimum. The English issue is dated 15 December 1957 and identifies the Russian original as June 1957. Full derivation remains open.

references.title: Pairing Symmetry and Flux Quantization in a Tricrystal Superconducting Ring of YBa2Cu3O7-delta

verification.note: Published 25 July 1994. The original abstract reports scanning SQUID observations at 4.2 K in rings with different junction counts. The complete original article and raw flux maps have not been reviewed here.

references.title: Spontaneous Supercurrent Induced by Ferromagnetic pi Junctions

verification.note: Published 26 May 2004; institutional upload 2009 is not publication. Selected final pages 1–4 were read for loop assumptions, Hall calibration, 2 K field sweeps and temperature-sweep subtraction. Page 2 was visually checked. Final Figure 4 gives approximately 5 K for spontaneous-current emergence, whereas author v1 said 5.5 K; neither is assigned as bulk Nb Tc. The final gamma sign and conventional-loop threshold differ from v1. The Wiki defines its own beta convention explicitly. Full device fitting and raw data remain open.

references.title: Theory of the Motion of Vortices in Superconductors

verification.note: Published 15 November 1965. Original abstract read for current-driven vortex motion, generated electric fields and flow resistivity in a local model. Full viscosity and Hall-response derivations were not reviewed.

claims.statement: A superconducting vortex is a defect of the real-space order parameter. For a single complex component that stays nonzero on a closed contour $C$, its phase winding is $n=(2\pi)^{-1}\oint_C\nabla\phi\cdot d\mathbf l\in\mathbb Z$. The contour must avoid cores and other zeros. Reversing its orientation reverses the sign; enclosing several defects gives their net winding. This integer is distinct from the momentum-space Chern number of a band or Bogoliubov Hamiltonian.
claims.conditions: Explicit charge/phase convention, nonzero order parameter on the contour, London or lumped-ring assumptions, junction geometry and sample-specific measurement criteria.
claims.verificationScope: Selected primary passages, original scans and bounded illustrations; complete scientific acceptance remains open.

claims.statement: Winding, fluxoid and measured magnetic flux answer different questions. Fluxoid combines magnetic flux with supercurrent circulation. A detector measures a geometry-dependent magnetic response, which need not equal the fluxoid around a chosen contour. Junction phase shifts and multicomponent textures require additional constraints; a fractional magnetic signal alone does not specify a new bulk condensate charge, Chern number or Majorana mode.

claims.statement: Use the explicit positive-charge phase convention $q=2e$, with $e\gt0$, and the local London relation $\mu_0\lambda_L^2\mathbf j_s=(\hbar/q)\nabla\phi-\mathbf A$. For constant $\lambda_L$ on the contour, integration gives $\Phi+\mu_0\lambda_L^2\oint_C\mathbf j_s\cdot d\mathbf l=n\Phi_0$, where $\Phi_0=h/(2e)\approx2.0678\times10^{-15}$ Wb. With a negatively charged pair-field convention, the associated phase winding reverses sign. These are equivalent conventions when used consistently. The simple constant-$\lambda_L$ expression assumes a local, uniform condensate response away from the core.

claims.statement: Only when the circulation term is negligible does magnetic flux itself approach $n\Phi_0$. A lumped uniform ring makes the distinction explicit: $I=(n\Phi_0-\Phi_{\rm ext})/(L_g+L_k)$, $\Phi=\Phi_{\rm ext}+L_gI$, and $\Phi+L_kI=n\Phi_0$. Here $L_g$ and $L_k$ are geometric and kinetic inductance. At zero applied flux with $n=1$ and $L_k=9L_g$, the magnetic flux is only $0.1\Phi_0$ although the fluxoid is one quantum. Twelve illustrative branches check this identity and the energy $(n\Phi_0-\Phi_{\rm ext})^2/[2(L_g+L_k)]$; they do not model phase-slip switching or an experimental device.

claims.statement: Twenty-four discrete phase-loop checks compare enclosed defect charges, contour reversal and smooth single-valued gauge changes at two resolutions. A contour intersecting a zero is rejected. These checks establish the numerical examples under the stated complex-field construction, not a classification of every superconducting order-parameter manifold. Singular gauge choices require separate treatment and were not tested.

claims.statement: For an ideal triangular array with one flux quantum per cell, $B(\sqrt3 a^2/2)=\Phi_0$ gives $a=\sqrt{2\Phi_0/(\sqrt3 B)}$. At mean induction $B=1$ T this is approximately $48.9$ nm. Four geometric checks verify the cell area; they do not establish that a particular sample has a triangular lattice. Use mean induction $B$, not applied field $H$ without a stated magnetization approximation. The later Abrikosov lecture favors the triangular array in the isotropic model but allows crystal-dependent alternatives; its result should not be attributed uncritically to the different early numerical estimate in the 1957 paper.

claims.statement: Deaver and Fairbank reported discrete trapped flux in tin cylinders consistent with $hc/2e$ in Gaussian units, including a first-step uncertainty of approximately 20 percent and explicit geometric corrections. Doll and Näbauer independently observed steps in lead-tube measurements, but their original report compared approximately 0.2 Oe spacing with 0.5 Oe predicted using $hc/e$ and left that discrepancy unresolved. Preserve the observations and uncertainties of each paper instead of rewriting both reports as identical precision determinations. The SI flux quantum has no factor of $c$.

claims.statement: Tsuei and colleagues reported spontaneous half-quantum flux in a three-junction YBCO tricrystal ring, absent in the two-junction controls, consistent with d-wave pairing. Their 4.2 K value is the scanning SQUID measurement temperature. Interpreting such a result requires the junction geometry and phase constraints, trapped-flux controls and a calibrated magnetic response; it is not an observation of an isolated half vortex in every ordinary single-component superconductor. The original abstract has been checked here, not the complete flux-map analysis.

claims.statement: Bauer and colleagues used niobium loops with PdNi ferromagnetic junctions and conventional-loop controls. Their final paper describes 2 K field sweeps, cooling-field reversal and subtraction of the Hall probe's temperature-dependent background; the low-temperature spontaneous flux approaches half a quantum. The final Figure 4 onset near 5 K replaces the author manuscript's approximate 5.5 K value. This is a device spontaneous-current scale, not a new bulk Nb transition temperature. Neither that onset nor the 2 K measurement is entered as experimental $T_c$.

claims.statement: Finite inductance matters even in a simple sinusoidal single-π-junction model. At zero applied field and negligible ring kinetic inductance, set $x=2\pi\Phi/\Phi_0$, $\beta_L=2\pi L_gI_c/\Phi_0$ with $I_c\gt0$, and normalized energy $u=x^2/2+\beta_L\cos x$. The stable nonzero solutions obey $x=\beta_L\sin x$ for $\beta_L\gt1$. Illustrative values $\beta_L=2,10,100$ give positive fluxes approximately $0.302,0.454,0.495$ quanta; at $0.5$ the minimum is zero. The half-quantum limit is approached with large $\beta_L$, not imposed exactly at every inductance. This independently checked model is distinct from the paper's gamma notation and from a multijunction tricrystal.

claims.statement: Store the contour, phase convention, inductive terms, field history, probe calibration and sample state alongside a vortex claim. Separate cell flux inferred from average induction, local sensor flux, fluxoid and momentum-space invariants. For a proposed fractional defect, identify the order-parameter or Josephson constraint and test competing trapped-flux explanations. These distinctions make a magnetic signal useful for comparing hypotheses without treating it as a complete pairing or topology diagnosis.

corrections.description: The original Doll–Näbauer report states an unresolved quantitative discrepancy using an hc/e prediction. Its exact result is retained rather than rewritten as an identical precision h/2e determination.
corrections.scope: Original pages 51–52 visually read; this is a correction to the pinned summary, not a rejection of historical flux quantization.

corrections.description: Restricted the vortex-transport paragraph to what the checked original abstract supports; removed the broader Nernst and pinning claims pending dedicated primary sources.
corrections.scope: Citation-scope correction; no assertion that the removed general statements are false.
